title: Functoriality of the maps on cohomology induced by f-maps
statement: Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_Y$-module, $\mathcal F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, $\varphi:\mathcal G\to h_*\mathcal F$ an $h$-map and $\varphi^*:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ ($p\ge0$) the map of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], with the cohomology groups of [pqf-def-cohomology]. (1) (Independence.) For a system of choices $C=(\mathcal I^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet,\mathcal J'^\bullet,\lambda,\beta)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap], with $\mu=\Gamma(Y,\lambda)$, put $\varphi^*_C=(\iota^p_{\mathcal I})^{-1}\circ H^p(\mu)^{-1}\circ H^p(\Gamma(Y,\beta))\circ\iota^p_{\mathcal J}$, where $\iota^p_{\mathcal I}:H^p(X,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$ and $\iota^p_{\mathcal J}:H^p(Y,\mathcal G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^\bullet))$ are the isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] for the global section functors $\Gamma(X,-)$ on $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\Gamma(Y,-)$ on $\mathcal O_Y$-modules (the identifications $H^p(X,\mathcal F)=H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))$, $H^p(Y,\mathcal G)=H^p(\Gamma(Y,\mathcal J^\bullet))$ of the definition). Then $\varphi^*_C=\varphi^*_{C'}$ for any two systems of choices $C$, $C'$. (2) (Composition.) Let $h:X\to Y$ and $k:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes, $\mathcal H$, $\mathcal G$, $\mathcal F$ modules on $Z$, $Y$, $X$, and $\psi:\mathcal H\to k_*\mathcal G$, $\varphi:\mathcal G\to h_*\mathcal F$ a $k$-map and an $h$-map. Then $k_*(\varphi)\circ\psi:\mathcal H\to k_*h_*\mathcal F=(k\circ h)_*\mathcal F$ is a $(k\circ h)$-map and $(k_*(\varphi)\circ\psi)^*=\varphi^*\circ\psi^*:H^p(Z,\mathcal H)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ for all $p\ge0$. In particular ($h$ or $k$ the identity) $\varphi^*\circ H^p(u)=(\varphi\circ u)^*$ and $H^p(v)\circ\varphi^*=(h_*(v)\circ\varphi)^*$ for morphisms of modules $u:\mathcal G'\to\mathcal G$ on $Y$ and $v:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ on $X$, $H^p(u)$, $H^p(v)$ the maps of the functors $H^p(Y,-)$, $H^p(X,-)$; and for the pullbacks [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (a) along $k$, $h$, $k\circ h$, $(k\circ h)^*=H^p(c)\circ h^*\circ k^*:H^p(Z,\mathcal H)\to H^p(X,(k\circ h)^*\mathcal H)$, where $c:h^*k^*\mathcal H\to(k\circ h)^*\mathcal H$ is the canonical comparison morphism of pullbacks [def-pc-module-pullback], i.e. the morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $(k\circ h)_*(c)\circ k_*(\eta^h_{k^*\mathcal H})\circ\eta^k_{\mathcal H}=\eta^{k\circ h}_{\mathcal H}$, $\eta^h,\eta^k,\eta^{k\circ h}$ the units of the adjunctions $h^*\dashv h_*$, $k^*\dashv k_*$, $(k\circ h)^*\dashv(k\circ h)_*$. (3) (Restriction.) Let $k:Y\to Z$, $\mathcal H$, $\mathcal G$, $\psi$ be as in (2), $V\subseteq Z$ open, $W=k^{-1}(V)$, $k|_W:W\to V$ the restricted morphism of open subschemes, and $\psi|_V:\mathcal H|_V\to(k|_W)_*(\mathcal G|_W)$ the morphism of $\mathcal O_V$-modules with components $\psi_T:\mathcal H(T)\to\mathcal G(k^{-1}T)$ for $T\subseteq V$ open (restricted modules as in [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]). Then $\mathrm{res}^Y_W\circ\psi^*=(\psi|_V)^*\circ\mathrm{res}^Z_V:H^p(Z,\mathcal H)\to H^p(W,\mathcal G|_W)$, with the restrictions of [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b).

proof.text: Independence: obtain a simultaneous homotopy comparison e between the auxiliary injective complexes. Apply additive global sections and homology to the two homotopies. Naturality of the canonical sections comparison gives m followed by q equals i followed by mprime, and beta gives b followed by q equals j followed by bprime. The resolution isomorphisms intertwine identity descent by isoRightDerivedObj_hom_naturality and mapHomologyIso_inv_naturality. Cancel mprime and the resolution isomorphisms to identify C.map with Cprime.map.

Composition: use the common-target section-homology diagram. ResolutionSectionsIso naturality supplies the three identity-descent squares. The private composition_diagram_cancel lemma first cancels the target resolution isomorphism and the invertible map mh followed by s. Use mc qc=i mh s and mk qk=g bh s to remove the inverse vertical maps; the beta square bc qc=j bk qk and source-resolution naturality finish the equality. Expand the definitions with explicit associativity simplification to transport it to Cc.map=Ck.map followed by Ch.map. Apply this proved helper to the three choices in moduleCohomologyFMap.

Source naturality: apply the composition clause with k the identity on Y and psi=a. The identity clause of moduleCohomologyFMap_basic_properties identifies the first cohomology map with H(a). On each open set the pushforward identity and composition comparison are identity maps, so extensionality identifies the composite module map with a followed by phi.

Target naturality: apply composition with h the identity on X, k the given scheme map, psi=phi, and the identity-scheme map b. Use the same identity clause to replace its cohomology map by H(b); check the pushforward composition comparison componentwise by reflexivity.

Pullback composition: unfold the pullback maps as maps of the adjunction units, reassociate, and use moduleCohomologyFMap_comp in reverse. Apply target naturality to c and use the supplied unit equation hc after reassociation. Thus the result follows from the strictly more general composition clause already in this module.

Restriction: define W=k inverse V, r=k restricted to W, and GV=G restricted to W. Form t=psi followed by the pushforward of the W-restriction unit and the pushforward composition comparison. Transpose t followed by the inverses of the scheme-equality and composition comparisons across the V-restriction adjunction to define psiV. The homEquiv apply-symm-apply identity and inverse cancellation prove the requested unit square. Rewrite both cohomology composites using moduleCohomologyFMap_comp. Equality transport in the scheme morphism, proved by elimination of its equality and the identity components of pushforwardCongr, identifies the two scheme composites. The unit square then proves the desired equality.

G2: composition reduced to a common-target diagram strictly before derived-resolution transport; all inverse cancellation and naturality transport are proved in the parent module. Independence cancellation is refactored into a private abstract diagram lemma to avoid unfolding concrete homology morphisms during rewriting.
